advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Derive used_fast_import from the actual code path taken (or drop the field) so its value and its test assertion reflect real execution.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_collapse.py:50: `used_fast_import: bool = True`
The field is never reassigned anywhere in collapse_shadow_tracker; CollapseResult(...) at line 158 omits used_fast_import so it keeps the constant default.
tests/unit/test_reclaim_collapse.py: `assert result.used_fast_import is True` cannot distinguish 'fast-import ran' from 'flag hardcoded True'.
advisory.finding: CollapseResult.used_fast_import is a hardcoded dataclass default (= True) that is never set from actual execution, so the test assertion `assert result.used_fast_import is True` is a tautology that would still pass even if the fast-import path never ran.
scenarios: A future refactor bypasses fast-import; the flag and its test still report success.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Let evaluation errors from checkpoint_commit_eligible surface as a distinct error rather than being coerced to a False 'ineligible' verdict.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_collapse.py:228-231: `try: return checkpoint_commit_eligible(...) except (OSError, ValueError, subprocess.SubprocessError): return False`
The caller at line 90-92 raises 'boundary ... is not eligible under the remote-anchored reclaim horizon' for a False return, conflating error with genuine ineligibility.
advisory.finding: _remote_horizon_eligible catches OSError/ValueError/SubprocessError and returns False; a genuine failure to evaluate eligibility is indistinguishable from a legitimately-ineligible boundary. While this fails closed (leads to refusal), it produces the misleading 'not eligible under the remote-anchored reclaim horizon' message for what is actually an evaluation error.
scenarios: git rev-parse of the remote ref fails transiently; user sees an eligibility refusal instead of the underlying error.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Read blob content by object id (git cat-file blob <oid>) instead of decoding the path, so non-UTF-8 tree paths do not crash.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_collapse.py:426: `return _git(tracker, "show", f"{treeish}:{path.decode()}", text=False).stdout`
_tree_entries keeps `path` as bytes and _quote_path handles non-UTF-8 via json.dumps, showing the design intends to tolerate non-UTF-8 paths.
advisory.finding: _blob_bytes_for_entry decodes the tree path as UTF-8 (`path.decode()`) and passes it through `git show <treeish>:<path>`, which will raise UnicodeDecodeError on a non-UTF-8 tree path — inconsistent with _tree_entries/_quote_path which deliberately handle path as raw bytes.
scenarios: A ticket file path with non-UTF-8 bytes causes an uncaught UnicodeDecodeError instead of a controlled error.
advisory.suggested_fix: Use the oid captured by _tree_entries: `_git(tracker, "cat-file", "blob", oid, text=False).stdout`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a signed/ledgered below-horizon entry (or a negative control that omits enforce_since) so test_enforce_since_reanchor_makes_verify_authorship_clean can only pass when re-anchoring actually rewrites the ledger anchor.
evidence: "authorship_ledger": [],
env sets "REBAR_IDENTITY_ENFORCE_SINCE": result.enforce_since
assert completed.returncode == 0, completed.stdout + completed.stderr
assert "OK" in (completed.stdout + completed.stderr)
ABSENCE: no assertion that verify-authorship FAILS when enforce_since is omitted or set to a pre-collapse value, so the test passes even if enforce_since re-anchoring is a no-op
advisory.finding: test_enforce_since_reanchor_makes_verify_authorship_clean uses an empty authorship_ledger, so verify-authorship would exit 0 whether or not enforce_since re-anchoring actually rewrote any ledger commit_sha. The test cannot detect a regression in the enforce_since re-anchoring behavior it claims to cover: with no signed/ledger entries below the horizon, the verify pass is trivially clean and there is no negative control proving it would fail without the returned enforce_since.
scenarios: enforce_since re-anchoring logic breaks (returns pre-rewrite anchor) yet the test stays green because the empty ledger makes verify trivially pass

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert exact collapsed_commits, replayed_commits, and ledger_entries_rewritten values on the multi-commit collapsible-store scenario.
evidence: original_count = int(_git(tracker, "rev-list", "--count", original_tip).stdout)
collapsed = max(0, original_count - len(commits))
ledger_rewrites += rewrites

ABSENCE: test_apply_collapses_below_horizon_history_and_preserves_reduced_state asserts rev-list count < 4 and used_fast_import is True but never asserts result.collapsed_commits, result.replayed_commits, or result.ledger_entries_rewritten
advisory.finding: The new CollapseResult observable counters collapsed_commits, replayed_commits, and ledger_entries_rewritten are computed by added logic (original_count - len(commits); ledger_rewrites accumulation) but no test asserts their concrete values on the multi-commit _build_collapsible_store scenario, leaving the count computation untested.
scenarios: off-by-one or sign error in collapsed_commits (e.g. max(0, ...) masking a negative) ships undetected
ledger_entries_rewritten accumulation double-counts or under-counts across replayed commits

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the ADR-0106 horizon eligibility check mandatory (or fail closed) rather than skipped when the remote-tracking horizon ref is absent from the shadow clone.
evidence: `if _has_remote_horizon_ref(tracker) and not _remote_horizon_eligible(tracker, boundary, now=now):` — the eligibility rejection only fires when the remote ref is present
comment at line 85-86: 'Enforce ADR-0106 eligibility when the shadow clone includes the copied remote-tracking horizon ref. Tiny offline fixtures may omit that ref'
`_has_remote_horizon_ref` returns False (line 234-244) when the ref is absent, short-circuiting the `and` so the collapse proceeds unchecked
test_remote_horizon_ref_makes_boundary_eligibility_blocking demonstrates the check is only 'blocking' once `refs/remotes/origin/tickets` is created — absent it, no horizon enforcement
advisory.finding: The ADR-0106 remote-horizon eligibility invariant is enforced only conditionally: it runs solely when `_has_remote_horizon_ref(tracker)` is true, so a shadow clone that lacks the remote-tracking ref bypasses the horizon guard entirely and can collapse an ineligible/too-recent boundary.
scenarios: A shadow clone created without copying the remote-tracking horizon ref collapses history that is not yet past the retention horizon, defeating the ADR-0106 invariant that below-horizon-only history is rewritten.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the live-tracker identity guard fail closed (refuse) instead of swallowing config-resolution errors with a bare `pass`.
evidence: `live = config.tracker_dir(None).resolve()` then `if live == tracker: raise ShadowSafetyError(...)` guarded by `except (config.ConfigError, OSError, RuntimeError): pass`
On any config-resolution failure the live-tracker identity comparison never runs, so this defense-in-depth guard is skipped rather than failing closed
advisory.finding: The 'refuse to rewrite the live configured tracker' safety guard fails open: if resolving the live tracker directory raises config.ConfigError/OSError/RuntimeError, the branch is silently swallowed (bare `pass`) and the identity check is skipped, allowing the collapse to proceed against a target that may be the live tracker.
scenarios: If config.tracker_dir cannot resolve (misconfigured env, transient OSError), the engine skips the live-tracker equality check; only the marker-file and no-remotes checks remain, so a marker-carrying clone that is actually the live tracker would not be caught by this specific guard.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the absence of the remote horizon ref an explicit decision (require it, or refuse/warn) rather than a silent bypass of the ADR-0106 eligibility gate.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_collapse.py:87: `if _has_remote_horizon_ref(tracker) and not _remote_horizon_eligible(`
Comment lines 85-86 acknowledge: 'Tiny offline fixtures may omit that ref; prod publishing remains S2.'
When the ref is absent the whole `and` short-circuits and no eligibility/age check is performed — a MISS path that is silent rather than an error.
blocking.finding: The ADR-0106 horizon-eligibility guard only runs when _has_remote_horizon_ref(tracker) is true; any shadow clone lacking the remote-tracking ticket ref silently skips the horizon check and collapses the boundary unconditionally, so an ineligible (too-recent) boundary is invisible rather than refused.
scenarios: A shadow clone created without copying refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch> collapses a boundary that is well within the reclaim horizon.
